key_insight: Bag-of-waves turns EEG into readable waveform tokens and their transitions, giving an interpretable, low-data alternative to black-box deep models.
clinical_relevance: This could support more transparent EEG analysis and biomarker discovery, especially when data are limited and clinicians need patterns they can inspect directly.
method: Learns a small dictionary of recurring EEG waveform atoms with shift-invariant k-means, without labels.
Encodes EEG as atom counts plus atom-to-atom n-grams to capture temporal structure.
Extends to multichannel regional and cross-channel spatial atoms for broader EEG settings.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on three datasets spanning low-data mouse clustering, resting-state dementia classification, and the TUEV clinical EEG event benchmark, where it was competitive with strong deep and foundation baselines.
watch_item: Performance is promising, but real-world adoption will depend on how well the learned atoms generalize across sites, montages, and patient populations.
paper_title: Interpretable EEG biomarkers with bag-of-waves: Spatial and temporal waveform dictionaries for low-data regimes
